newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexico crude ports shut amid high winds - ports.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexico crude ports shut amid high winds - ports.

text.p: Two Mexican crude ports, Pajaritos and Dos Bocas, were reported closed on Wednesday as a sudden storm hit the northern Gulf of Mexico, port authority officials said.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state shut at 1245 local/1745 GMT and Pajaritos in Veracruz state closed at 1100 local/1600 GMT, officials told Reuters.
Port officials said winds rose up to 65 km per hour in the area, with waves seven to nine feet high.
The storm had died down mid-afternoon and the ports could reopen at 1700 local/2200 GMT, officials said.
A cold front in the region closed five ports on Wednesday, according to the latest meteorological bulletin from the Communications and Transport Ministry.
The third and largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open to crude shipments despite the strong winds, a port official said.
He said two ships were being loaded with crude mid-afternoon.

Cayo Arcas ships an average 611,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, while Dos Bocas ships 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos ships 399,000 bpd, according to the latest figures from state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
